chapter: Ellington band members and life on the road
title: Mistaking Benny Waters for Benny Carter at Charlie Johnson's
summary: Sitting in with Charlie Johnson's band, Bigard took Benny Waters for Benny Carter, judged him unimpressive, then met the real Carter, who was arranging in the back, and was embarrassed.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: That's where I first met Benny Carter.

See, when I worked at the Nest with Luis Russell, well, that was Charlie Johnson's band -- that was his second band. He booked Luis in there, see? And when I worked with -- Charlie wanted me to come in his band, the big band, like the mother band, as you would say, and I didn't want to leave Luis. So then I'd go there sometime and sit in, you know.

So the funny part about the night I went to sit in, I wanted to meet this -- I heard so much about this Benny Carter so much I wanted to meet him and hear him play. So I took the night off and I went over to Charlie Johnson -- No, I went early. That's what it was. Because we didn't go -- I didn't go -- we didn't start work till about 11 o'clock. Then I went over there and I sat in. And the guy next to me, his name was Benny Waters, but I -- just that fast I didn't grasp the name Waters. I thought it was Benny Carter.

So I listened. I thought, oh, he's not much. I don't think so much of him. In the meantime Benny Carter was in the back making an arrangement for the band. So after that set, here comes Benny Carter. I still don't know it's Benny Carter. So he's coming now, he's giving me this jive, you know. 'Oh, wow, where'd you learn all that stuff from? Who taught you all that? Where you from?' I'm telling him where I'm from and I'm proud of myself, you know. So finally this

Benny Waters said, "Have you met him?" I said, "No, who is he?" He said, "That's Benny Carter." I said, "Oh, it is." Boy, I felt about that low, you know. And he had finished that arrangement, so I put my horn away and went to sit down and listen, and when I heard I walked out.
I says, oh, God. I wasn't getting messed up in this. It was so fantastic.
So Benny was what, arranging and playing for that band?
